chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: Why they endured the hard life
summary: Smith says musicians did it for fun and status, staying at teachers' and professionals' houses.

blocks.x: Again, coming back to the Blue Devils and all this touring
around. The life you describe was very tough, very hard.
And apparently not very well paid.
You must have loved it. Why did you do it?
Well, most of the musicians, just for the fun of it.

Yeah. Having a good time. You know, they didn't have a whole lot money in their pocket. They were havin' a good time. Meanwhile, they were getting their shoes shined, had a car in town. It was part of being a professional. Same kind of (?) as a lawyer or a doctor or something like that. We went to town, that's where we stayed. We always stayed at some uptown people's houses, somebody who was a professional -- stayed there because we were supposed to be of the same caliber. But in later years, it got so it got to be a drag, so you couldn't hardly get a room in a hotel.
I see. But in the early days...
In the early days, that's what...
You were somebody, is what you're saying.
Oh yes. Schoolteacher's house; stay at the schoolteacher's house. Yeah. Sure did. Yessir.
